profile.reading: Per CyrusOne own facility page for Quincy, Washington (PNW1), this facility publishes 36 MW of total IT capacity and 720,000 square feet of technical IT space, at a street address of 1025 D Street Northwest, Quincy, WA 98848. CyrusOne describes the site as located about halfway between Seattle and Spokane, and as the largest greenfield built facility the company has developed in Washington state, with additional land reserved for future development subject to power availability.

reading.body:
CyrusOne PNW1 publishes 36 MW of IT capacity across 720,000 square feet of technical space in Quincy, Washington. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 36 MW is roughly 900 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a legacy colocation density, the same power supports around 3,600 racks. The arithmetic is an interpretive range, not an operator claim. No certifications are listed on the spec page, so none can be read for what workload tiers the campus qualifies to host.

Quincy sits in Grant County, where the Columbia River hydroelectric system has historically kept power cheap and carbon-light, but nothing about grid contracts, power cost, or stranded capacity is published on this spec page, so those factors cannot be assessed from the data. The 720,000-square-foot technical footprint is large relative to the 36 MW figure, implying an average density of 50 watts per square foot across the technical space, which is on the lower end for a purpose-built AI facility and suggests the campus was designed or filled for lower-density workloads, or that significant space is underutilized or unequipped.

Among the 46 data center facilities mapped in Washington State, PNW1 is the only one for which an operator spec page has yielded a published megawatt figure, making it rank first in the state by published IT capacity with a 100 percent share of the state's published total. That ranking reflects a data gap more than a market reality: 45 other mapped facilities in Washington publish no capacity figure this site has read, so the state total of 36 MW is a floor, not a ceiling.
